content:
The [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. See how savings grow with compounding and monthly deposits. Enter your initial deposit, monthly contribution, annual interest rate, years and compounding and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Compound interest is interest earned on both your original money and the interest it has already earned. Over long periods it's the single biggest driver of investment growth. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the Compound Interest Calculator

Start by entering your initial deposit, then entering your monthly contribution, entering your annual interest rate (%), entering your years and finally choosing your compounding from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your initial deposit.
2. Enter your monthly contribution.
3. Enter your annual interest rate (%).
4. Enter your years.
5. Choose your compounding from the list.
6. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.

## Formula

A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), plus the future value of regular contributions. P is the principal, r the annual rate, n compounding periods per year, t the years.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 10,000 plus 200 a month at 7% compounded monthly grows to about 91,000 after 15 years — more than 35,000 of that is interest. Try the same figures in the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Initial deposit: 10000, Monthly contribution: 200, Annual interest rate: 7 %, Years: 15, Compounding: Monthly), the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) returns Future value: 91,881.93, Total contributed: 46,000, Interest earned: 45,881.93. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Start early: time matters more than the amount.
- Reinvest dividends and interest.
- Use the Rule of 72 — 72 ÷ rate ≈ years to double.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What's the difference between simple and compound interest?

Simple interest is paid only on the principal; compound interest is also paid on accumulated interest. Try it with your own numbers in the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does compounding frequency matter?

Yes, slightly. Daily compounding earns a little more than monthly, which earns more than yearly. Try it with your own numbers in the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Compound Interest Calculator use?

A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), plus the future value of regular contributions. P is the principal, r the annual rate, n compounding periods per year, t the years. You can see it in action in the [Compound Interest Calculator](/compound-interest-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

Just Initial deposit, Monthly contribution, Annual interest rate, Years and Compounding. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
